name: mycrew
description: mycrew — a five-layer harness for Claude Code, each layer built on the one below. 1) mycrew-tools gives you the primitives and the house rules. 2) mycrew-pipeline is the build pipeline that carries a task from a decision to hardened code. 3) mycrew-worker is the executor that drives the pipeline on one project. 4) mycrew-product is the product plane — what the product must do and how it is built, drawn out of you and written down in one place. 5) mycrew-chief sits on top as your deputy: it shapes that plane and orchestrates workers across the sub-projects. Install mycrew-tools first.

plugins.name: mycrew-tools
plugins.description: Layer 1/5 — primitives. Small, project-agnostic skills you or the model reach for while working: /slap resets a stuck fix, /likec4 draws C4 architecture-as-code, /reminder pins one rule file as a hard constraint, /retract hunts down information declared wrong and surgically removes it. Also ships the harness's rule files (rules/) to copy into a project's .claude/rules/. The primitives every layer above builds on.

plugins.name: mycrew-pipeline
plugins.description: Layer 2/5 — the build pipeline. Six stage skills that carry one task from a decision to hardened code: /how-to-do (decide a fork), /do (build it by a tight set of writing rules), then /refactor (clean it and reuse what exists), /review (edge cases and bugs), /secure (the holes) and /test to harden and ship it. In /review and /secure the eyes that hunt and the eyes that rule are never the author's — only the fixes are. Every stage gates itself: it judges what actually changed against its own bar and skips in one honest line when the change doesn't earn it, so nothing is picked by guesswork and every skip is named. Skills only. Built on mycrew-tools; driven by mycrew-worker.

plugins.name: mycrew-worker
plugins.description: Layer 3/5 — the executor. Hand /worker one piece of work (a fix, a change, a feature, a question) and it carries it to the end: every fork inside that work it settles itself, splitting the job across its own subagents when that pays — and it never widens the brief. Anything outside comes back as a flag in its report, in plain human language, and so does anything the design got wrong: it builds to the plane and never writes it. It takes no flags and creates no report file: the work ends with a fixed four-part answer to whoever dispatched it — what got done, which forks it settled and how, which instruments it used, what it left outside the brief. Runs inline as /worker or as a native subagent the chief dispatches. Built on mycrew-pipeline + mycrew-tools.

plugins.name: mycrew-product
plugins.description: Layer 4/5 — the product plane: everything true about the whole product, in one repository above the sub-projects. /product-init founds it (the folder holding your sub-project repos becomes its own git repo, with a North Star drawn from you). Two endless modes then draw the product out of you and file each affirmed piece where it lives: /braindump listens while you unload and never steers, /ask-me questions you one angle at a time until the product is thought through. Both are strictly extractive — your vision and never its own; propose-idea is the one counterpart, inventing a feature, pitching it with the case for it, and filing it only on your approval. The plane's two views and the rules they obey live here: product-view for docs/product/ (what the product must do — one line per feature and nothing beneath it, with the full picture of any feature that needs one in its own file beside the list, in your words; plus the work no feature covers and what was settled and why) and design-view for docs/design/ (the one model.c4 tree and the technical choices beside it). /look-ahead is what fills that design view before the code exists — one pass over the whole plane at once instead of feature by feature, so building step by step never locks in an architecture nobody chose: it settles only what would be expensive to reverse, says what it deliberately left open, reports what the features turned out to demand of each other, and writes nothing until you have approved it. why-do-it is the gate before work starts: anything whose rightness isn't obvious goes through it and comes back GO or NO-GO with the real problem named and the better route, if there is one. pitch is the way back out: it reads the whole plane and tells you how your product works — one plain story, strictly what is written, closing with what the plane couldn't answer. Built on mycrew-tools; driven by mycrew-chief.

plugins.name: mycrew-chief
plugins.description: Layer 5/5 — the top layer, the human's deputy over the whole product. /chief reads the plane the product layer holds — what the product must do and how it is built — shapes it as the human's deputy, decomposes an approved feature into per-repo assignments, picks what to advance next (what-to-do), gates anything doubtful before it becomes code (the product layer's why-do-it — the real problem, the alternatives, assume it failed, GO or NO-GO), sequences and dispatches workers as native subagents (worker-orchestration), and takes or sends back what comes home (accept-work — the brief it sent against the report that came back, ACCEPTED or BACK; only accepted work moves the plane). It never decides what the product should do — that stays the human's — and it never writes code. It conducts; the workers build. Built on mycrew-product + mycrew-worker.
